body:
## What to build

Change `log.sh`'s auto format detection and color detection from live `test -t <fd>` to a startup-cached `_LOG_IS_TTY`, so that once the always-on transcript tee (later slice) redirects fd1, the terminal's format/color decision still follows the user's real terminal rather than being polluted by the internal tee. Keep a fallback: when `_LOG_IS_TTY` is unset, fall back to live `test -t`, so sourcing `log.sh` standalone (e.g. from ci.sh) behaves unchanged.

In the same PR write ADR `doc/adr/00000007` covering three points: the rationale for the TTY-cache revision of the #438 single-sink semantics; the layering of the transcript tee on top of single-sink; and the best-effort mixed format of the transcript file under `LOG_FORMAT=json` (no dual-render, since the mixed format originates from the docker child-process output). Establish `CONTEXT.md` as a glossary and add the terms "Single-sink dispatch" and "Run trace id".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_log_dispatch`'s auto branch and `_log_color_enabled` read `_LOG_IS_TTY`, falling back to live detection when unset
- [ ] With `_LOG_IS_TTY=0`, output is JSON even when stdout is a tty; with `_LOG_IS_TTY=1`, text is forced
- [ ] Sourcing `log.sh` standalone (not via _lib.sh) behaves identically to before the revision
- [ ] ADR 00000007 written; CONTEXT.md glossary established and contains the two terms above
- [ ] Adjust existing log bats + add cache-behavior specs; sync CHANGELOG

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately
title: feat: single-sink TTY-cache revision (#438) + ADR 00000007
